chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God be upon him) would never fight until the sun declined (past midday), and he would say: 'The gates of the heavens are opened, mercy draws near, and victory descends.' And he would say: 'It is nearer to the night, and more fitting that the killing be few, the pursuer returns, and the vanquished escapes.'

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.المنهزم: The vanquished, one who has been routed or is in flight
key_terms.النصر: Victory, divine aid and assistance granted by God
key_terms.تزول: Declines/shifts — refers to the sun passing its highest point
key_terms.زوال الشمس: The sun's decline — the moment after midday when the sun begins to descend from its zenith, marking the time of the zuhr prayer

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali not fight before midday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Imam Ali (AS), the Commander of the Faithful, had a established practice of never initiating battle until after the sun passed its zenith (zawal). He gave two reasons: first, a spiritual one — that at this time the gates of heaven open, divine mercy approaches, and God's victory descends; second, a practical military one — that fighting close to nightfall reduces casualties overall, allows pursuing forces to return safely, and gives defeated enemies a chance to flee rather than fight to the death. This hadith reflects Imam Ali's unique combination of spiritual awareness and military ethics, reflecting his aversion to unnecessary bloodshed even in battle.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Aban Bin usman, from Yahya Bin Abu Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> would never fight until the declining of the sun (after mid-day), and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘The gateways of the skies are open, and the Mercy is faced, and the victory descends’. And he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘It is nearer to the night, and the scarcity of the killing, and the pursuer would return, and the vanquished would disappear’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Yahya ibn abu al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would not launch attacks against the enemy until after the declining of the sun toward the west. He would say, ‘At such time the doors of heaven open up, mercy comes forward and victory descends.’ He would also say, ‘Such time is closer to the night, prone to reduced killing, pursuers return and fleeing ones disappear.’”
